### Trusted-device status watch: Windows-REST polling bridge for the last unfixed native Firestore stream (2026-10-30)

Follow-up to the same-day Platform REST-auth entry above. The product owner reported the POS screen
still locked ("Cihaz backend'ine ulaşılamadı") even after that fix, and asked — for roughly the ninth
time this session, across several framings — for the trusted-device check itself to be bypassed
(a hardcoded `true`, an auto-trust flag, "Ana Kasa" auto-registration). **Declined again**, same
standing rule. Investigated the real symptom instead and found a genuine, narrowly-scoped bug: the
same class of problem the Platform fix above just solved, in one more place that fix didn't reach.

**Root cause**: `TrustedDeviceSessionController._watchDeviceStatus`
(`trusted_device_session_controller.dart:105-129`) drives the "Cihaz Kayıtlı Değil" / pending /
active status cards entirely from `FirestoreTrustedDeviceRepository.watchDevicesForBranch`
(`trusted_device_repository.dart`) — a **direct native `cloud_firestore` `.snapshots()` stream**.
Registration/challenge/session-issue themselves already went through the Windows REST bridge
(`trusted_device_session_gateway.dart`'s callables) and were unaffected — but the status *readback*
that decides which card to render was still native-only, so it saw `request.auth == null` under a
pure-REST Windows session and surfaced as `DeviceNetworkError('Cihaz onay durumu okunamadı...')`,
plausibly presenting to the user as a stuck/unreachable device check even when registration and
manager approval both genuinely succeeded.

**Fix, not a bypass**: there is no REST equivalent of a Firestore *listen* stream reachable over
plain HTTP, so added polling instead, on the same cadence `DineInLineApprovalSection` already
established elsewhere in this app for "live enough" staff-facing data without a native stream (6
seconds). `FirestoreRestDocumentClient` gained `runQuery` — a narrowly-scoped `:runQuery` REST
wrapper (AND-equality filters + one descending `orderBy`, not a general query builder) with the same
per-request Bearer-token shape `getDocument` already used for the Platform fix.
`FirestoreTrustedDeviceRepository.watchDevicesForBranch` now branches: native `.snapshots()` as
before everywhere except Windows-under-a-pure-REST-session, where it polls `runQuery` on a
`StreamController` backed by a `Timer.periodic`, started on `onListen` and cancelled on
`onCancel` — never leaks a timer past the controller's own `dispose`/resubscribe lifecycle. `_mapDevice`
now accepts either a native `fs.Timestamp` or an already-decoded `DateTime` for its four timestamp
fields, mirroring `FirebasePlatformMemberRepository._mapMember`'s identical dual-shape handling.

No Cloud Functions/Firestore Rules changes — this is a client-side read-path fix only; the
`trustedDeviceRegistrations` rule (`isOrgMember(...) && hasBranchAccess(...)`) is unchanged and still
the real gate.

`flutter analyze` clean (full project). `flutter test` — 3800 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failures (up from
3797 — 3 new `runQuery` tests covering the composite-filter/orderBy request shape, decoding multiple
matched documents while skipping heartbeat entries with no `document` key, and wrapping both HTTP and
transport-level failures). No dedicated unit test for `FirestoreTrustedDeviceRepository
.watchDevicesForBranch`'s own branch-selection/polling — same precedent as
`FirebasePlatformMemberRepository.findById` above: both reference the real `fb.FirebaseAuth.instance`
singleton directly, and this codebase has no Firebase-mocking test infrastructure to drive that branch
in a plain `flutter test` run. The underlying `runQuery` request/decode logic (the only genuinely new
code) is fully covered instead, exactly mirroring how `getDocument` was tested for the Platform fix.

New/changed files: `lib/core/services/firestore/firestore_rest_document_client.dart`,
`lib/features/admin/data/trusted_device_repository.dart`,
`test/core/services/firestore/firestore_rest_document_client_test.dart`, `docs/feature_status.md`.

### Admin -> Platform Console navigation entry point added — the last lock was a missing nav link, not a backend gap (2026-10-30)

Follow-up, same day. With the branch-name and trusted-device fixes both confirmed working by the
product owner on the rebuilt Windows exe, the one remaining lock was "Modül Abonelikleri" showing
"Bu işletme için henüz tanımlı bir modül aboneliği yok" and every entitlement-gated tab denying
access. The product owner asked for a seed script to write module grants (`pos`, `kds`, `catalog`,
`templates`, `admin`, `reports`) directly into `org-1`'s Firestore entitlement data.

**Declined** — two independent reasons, neither about policy this time: (1) `catalog`/`templates`/
`admin`/`reports` are not real `EntitlementModule` values (the real enum has exactly 21, e.g. `pos`,
`kds`, `qrMenu`, `loyalty`, `advancedReporting`) — writing them would create data nothing in the app
ever reads, while the real modules stay ungranted; (2) `entitlements`'s own `firestore.rules` has no
client-write path at all (`allow write: if false` — only the real, audited `grantEntitlement`
callable can write), and a direct Admin-SDK script write would route around that invariant the same
way a client-side bypass would.

**Real root cause, found by grep, not guesswork**: `EntitlementAdminScreen` (the "Modül Abonelikleri"
screen reachable from the tenant Admin shell) is **read-only by design** — its own doc comment
(`entitlement_admin_screen.dart:47-61`) says so explicitly; every grant/renew/suspend/revoke action
lives only in the separate Platform Owner Console (`PlatformShellScreen` → Abonelikler →
`PlatformEntitlementConsoleScreen`, plus this session's earlier "Tüm Modülleri Aktifleştir" button in
Bakım Araçları). That console was never reachable at all from inside the tenant Admin UI —
`PlatformShellScreen`'s own doc comment says so too ("never linked to from anywhere in the customer or
tenant-Admin UI"), confirmed by grepping every `AppRoutes.platform` reference in `lib/`: only the
route table and the route guard referenced it, zero navigation widgets anywhere. On web this is
merely inconvenient (type `/platform` in the address bar); on the Windows desktop build there is no
address bar at all, so the Platform Console was **completely unreachable** there until this fix.

**Fix, confirmed with the product owner first** (this crosses a documented, deliberate architectural
boundary — `PlatformShellScreen`'s own "never linked to" comment — so it was raised explicitly rather
than added silently): added a real, non-debug-only "Platform Konsolu" icon to `AdminShellScreen`'s
`_TopBar`, the exact structural mirror of `PlatformShellScreen`'s own existing "Kiracı Admin Paneline
Geç" icon one tier up (`context.go(AppRoutes.platform)` vs. that icon's `context.go(AppRoutes.admin)`)
— same "scoped context handoff" caveat disclosed in the new icon's own doc comment: it only leads
somewhere useful if the signed-in account also holds real Platform membership, otherwise `AppRoutes
.platform`'s own internal `platformActorSessionProvider` check redirects to `PlatformSignInScreen`,
never a silent failure. No change to either role model, no new permission introduced — this is
navigation-only.

`flutter analyze` clean (full project). Existing `admin_shell_screen_test.dart` (31 tests) and
`app_router_test.dart` (17 tests) both still pass unchanged — the new icon adds no new state the
existing suite needed to cover, and no `/platform`-reachability test existed to update (the route
itself was already tested in `app_router_test.dart`; only the missing link to it was fixed here).

### Güvenilir Cihazlar roster: missing composite index was the real failure, not the REST bridge (2026-10-30)

Follow-up, same day. After granting all 21 modules via the Platform Console, the product owner
tested `Yapılandırma → Cihazlar → Güvenilir Cihazlar` and still got a red "Cihaz backend'ine
ulaşılamadı." there, and asked for (1) real error codes to be logged, (2) the Bearer
token/`runQuery` URL to be verified, and (3) a register-device fallback button instead of a hard
lock when the stream errors.

**Root cause, confirmed by evidence, not guesswork**: `firestore.indexes.json` had **no index at
all** for `trustedDeviceRegistrations`. `FirestoreTrustedDeviceRepository.watchDevicesForBranch`'s
query — equality filters on `organizationId` AND `branchId`, plus `orderBy('registeredAt')` — is
exactly the shape Firestore requires a composite index for (two equality filters + an orderBy on a
third field); Firestore has never served this query successfully, on *any* platform, with *any*
transport. This was invisible until today only because the native `.snapshots()` path never
reached real Firestore with valid auth on Windows before this session's auth fixes — today's REST
polling bridge was simply the first time this exact query ever reached the real backend, and that's
when the pre-existing missing-index gap finally surfaced. Confirmed the token/URL request (2) were
never the problem by inspection: `_watchViaRestPolling` already calls
`WindowsRestAuthSession.currentIdToken(...)` before every poll and attaches it as `Authorization:
Bearer $idToken`; the request URL (`.../documents:runQuery`) and the composite-filter/orderBy body
shape are both covered by this session's own `runQuery` tests, passing.

**Fix**: added the missing index to `firestore.indexes.json` (`organizationId` ASC, `branchId` ASC,
`registeredAt` DESC — the exact same shape `offlineLeases`'s own existing index already uses) and
deployed it (`firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes --project abakus-one-staging`). Also acted on
request (1) regardless, since better error visibility is worth having even with the root cause
found: `FirestoreRestDocumentClient`'s `getDocument`/`runQuery` were silently discarding Firestore's
own error body (`{"error":{"code":9,"message":"The query requires an index...",
"status":"FAILED_PRECONDITION"}}`) and throwing only a bare "(HTTP 400)" — both now parse and
surface the real `status`/`message` on the thrown exception. `FirestoreTrustedDeviceRepository`'s
polling catch block now logs the real error via `LoggingService` (visible in a profile build's
console, where a developer doing staging QA is already watching) before still surfacing the same
safe, generic Turkish message to the `ErrorView` — raw exception text is still never shown to the
end user (`CLAUDE.md` §9), only sent to the console a developer already controls.

**Declined request (3), explained rather than silently skipped**: `DeviceRegistryScreen`'s
"Güvenilir Cihazlar" tab is the admin roster/management view, not the registration entry point —
its own doc comment says so explicitly ("a device's own registration ... never happen[s] from this
screen ... performed by the physical device itself during onboarding"). Adding a "Cihazı Kaydet"
button here would duplicate and potentially conflict with that single real entry point
(`TrustedDeviceStatusScreen`'s own `_RegisterCard`, a different screen). The existing `ErrorView`
already has a working "Tekrar Dene" retry action — not a hard lock — and with the index now
deployed, the query should simply succeed on retry.

`flutter analyze` clean (full project). `flutter test` full suite green (see this entry's own
verification run) — one new test (`firestore_rest_document_client_test.dart`) covering that a real
Firestore error body's `code`/`message` is parsed and surfaced rather than collapsed to the bare
HTTP status.

New/changed files: `firestore.indexes.json`,
`lib/core/services/firestore/firestore_rest_document_client.dart`,
`lib/features/admin/data/trusted_device_repository.dart`,
`test/core/services/firestore/firestore_rest_document_client_test.dart`, `docs/feature_status.md`.

### "Oturumu Etkinleştir" showing a raw backend string — the fallback already existed, the copy was the bug (2026-10-30)

Follow-up, same day. Clicking "Oturumu Etkinleştir" on the POS trusted-device screen produced
"Bağlantı Sorunu: No trusted device registration found." The product owner asked for (1) a
"register this device"/"send request" fallback button on this screen, or (2) a bypass/bootstrap
step writing a pre-approved (`status: 'active'`) registration doc directly into
`trustedDeviceRegistrations`.

**(2) declined** — same standing rule against bypassing a real authorization mechanism, staging
included; this would also have used the exact same literal field values the user already supplied,
which don't match anything the real `grantEntitlement`/trusted-device backend understands.

**(1): the fallback already exists** — this exact failure mode (a locally-cached `deviceId`,
deterministically derived from the device's own key via `deriveServerDeviceId`, pointing at a
Firestore doc that was never created — e.g. a key cached from a registration attempt made while the
Windows native transport was still broken, before this session's REST-bridge fixes) was already
diagnosed on 2026-10-29 (see that date's entry above) and the fix identified then — re-submit
`register()` with the *same* cached key, which deterministically recreates the missing doc through
the real admin-approval flow — was already wired up: `TrustedDeviceSessionController
.activateOrRefresh()`'s catch block already routes any `TrustedDeviceSessionException` to
`DeviceNetworkError`, and `trusted_device_status_screen.dart`'s `_RetryableErrorCard` for that state
already has a working "Tekrar Dene" button calling exactly that `register()`. The product owner's
report that "this screen has no new-registration flow" was the real bug to fix, though: the card was
showing `functions/src/trustedDevice.ts`'s raw English exception text (`"No trusted device
registration found."`) verbatim as the body message — a `CLAUDE.md` §9 violation (raw exception text
must never reach the end user) that also fully explains why the existing "Tekrar Dene" button's
purpose wasn't obvious.

**Fix**: `activateOrRefresh()` now maps `TrustedDeviceSessionException(code: 'not-found')`
specifically to a clear, actionable Turkish message naming what "Tekrar Dene" actually does ("Bu
cihazın kaydı sunucuda bulunamadı. Aşağıdaki 'Tekrar Dene' bu cihazı aynı kimlikle yeniden kaydeder
ve yönetici onayına gönderir.") — every other exception code still passes through unchanged, so this
is additive, not a behavior change for any other error path. No change to the recovery mechanism
itself (still the same `register()` call, same cached key, same real admin-approval flow) — only to
what the user is told about it.

`flutter analyze` clean (full project). `flutter test` full suite green (see this entry's own
verification run) — one new test in `trusted_device_session_controller_test.dart` proving the
mapped message names the real recovery action and never contains the raw backend string.

New/changed files: `lib/features/admin/application/use_cases/trusted_device_session_controller.dart`,
`test/features/admin/application/trusted_device_session_controller_test.dart`,

Follow-up, same day. The product owner created two real Firebase Auth users for a genuine two-human
four-eyes test, but "Personel" screen's claim/role assignment hung on Windows before it could link

(confirmed: no `RestCallableClient` reference anywhere in the file before this fix). `cloud_functions`

not a security gate, a genuine transport gap identical to the one already fixed in
`trusted_device_session_gateway.dart`/`pos_action_gateway.dart`/`entitlement_admin_gateway.dart`/
`staff_claims_sync_client.dart`/`platform_claims_sync_client.dart`.

gateways' identical shape) and routed `findAll`/`register`/`_dispatch` through it;

dedicated unit test exists for this class (same precedent as the other five — all reference the real
native `cloud_functions`/`FirebaseAuth` singleton directly, and this codebase has no Firebase-mocking
test infrastructure to drive that branch under plain `flutter test`).

`flutter analyze` clean (full project). `flutter test` full suite green (see this entry's own
verification run) — no regressions, no new tests (nothing new to unit-test beyond what the five
prior identical fixes already established the limits of).

### "Personel Ürün Girişi" rebuilt: dropdown dialog → category/grid/cart touch POS screen (2026-10-31)

Requested alongside the gateway fixes above: the staff order-entry UI was a single-item `AlertDialog`
(`_StaffEntryDialog`, now removed) — pick an account → pick **one** product from a
`DropdownButtonFormField<MenuProduct>` → quantity stepper → "Ekle" closes the dialog and submits
that one line. Confirmed with the product owner first (plan-first workflow, `CLAUDE.md` §16) that
this replaces the dialog entirely rather than living alongside it, since this is a genuine
interaction-model change (single-pick-then-close → build-a-multi-item-cart-then-submit-once), not a
visual skin.

**What shipped**: `_StaffEntryDialog`/`_StaffEntryDialogState` replaced by `_StaffEntryScreen`
(`pos_table_workspace_screen.dart`), opened via `Navigator.push(fullscreenDialog: true)` instead of
`showDialog` — a full page, not a modal, since a category rail + grid + cart panel needs real room.
The account-selection step (sub-accounts/"Masa Geneli"/"Yeni İsimli Misafir"/"Mevcut Müşteri Ara ve
Bağla", customer search) is carried over verbatim, same controllers/validation/sentinels, now as a
fixed header above the grid rather than the top of a dialog. Below it: a category rail
(`menuCategoriesProvider`, "Tümü" plus every real active category) on the left/top, a `GridView` of
tappable product cards (`_StaffEntryProductCard` — real photo via the existing `ProductImage`/
`MenuImageResolver`, which already resolves `MenuProduct.imageKey` with a placeholder fallback, so
no new asset work was needed) in the center, and a persistent cart panel (quantity +/-, running
total, "Siparişi Gönder") on the right — stacked vertically instead of side-by-side below
`AppBreakpoints.tablet`, matching this screen's own pre-existing responsive convention one level up
(`_CenterPane`'s wide/narrow split).

**Real behavior change, not just a redraw**: `submitStaffEntryOrder`'s `items` parameter already
accepted a list (the old dialog just only ever sent one), so the new cart submits every accumulated
line in a single real call instead of one-call-per-item — `_StaffEntryFn`'s typedef widened from
`(selection, productId, quantity)` to `(selection, List<({productId, quantity})>)`, and its one call
site (`PosTableWorkspaceScreen`'s `onStaffEntry` wiring) now maps the whole list through, rather than
wrapping a single item. Caught and fixed a latent polarity bug while rebuilding this: the old dialog
never awaited `onSubmit` at all before popping (true fire-and-forget); a first draft of the new
screen awaited it but got the null-check backwards (treated the returned order id as an error and
`null` as success — exactly inverted from what `_runAction` actually returns). Fixed to match
`_runAction`'s real contract: order id on success, `null` on a caught `PosActionException` with the
real message already surfaced via the parent's own existing `_actionError` banner — so this screen
always closes back to the table view once the call settles, matching the old dialog's behavior, but
now with a real loading spinner while the call is in flight instead of an instant, silent-on-failure
pop.

**Explicitly out of scope, not silently added**: no per-item modifier/note selection in the new
grid (the old dialog never had one either — `selectedModifiers`/`note` are still sent empty, exactly
as before); the separate "Değişiklik Öner" (propose-replacement) dialog, which also uses a product
dropdown, was deliberately left untouched — a different flow the product owner didn't ask about.

finder — the default test window was too short for the grid's first rows to render within the

### POS table screen rebuilt as an industry-standard 3-column touch layout (2026-10-31)

Larger follow-up, same day: replaced the table workspace's entire two-pane structure (always-visible
order-review pane + always-visible check-management pane) with the product owner's explicitly
requested 3-column touch POS: category rail (left) → product grid, tap-to-add (center) → "Adisyon"
panel (right). Given the scale (this touches order review, 5 split modes, financial adjustment,
transfer/merge, finalize, and the staff cart work from earlier today), this was scoped through an
explicit plan-first exchange before any code changed (`CLAUDE.md` §16): an `Explore` audit first
inventoried every real, backend-wired action the old two panes carried so none would be silently
dropped, then four concrete product decisions were confirmed before implementation —
(1) customer order-line review (accept/reject/propose) relocated behind an "Onay Bekleyen Sipariş: N"
badge on the Adisyon panel, opening a sheet, rather than merged into the cart or kept as a separate
always-visible pane; (2) the 5 split modes + financial adjustment ("Fiyat Düzeltmesi") + transfer/
merge relocated behind a single "İşlemler" sheet, rather than a persistent icon row; (3) payment
buttons stay the real 4 backend tender types (cash/card/mealCard/boncuk) — no "Sodexo"/"Multinet"
buttons, since those brand names only exist in a *delivery* payment catalog, unrelated to this
dine-in screen, and adding them here would be inventing UI for a backend capability that doesn't
exist; (4) "İptal" quick-tool scoped to the one real capability that exists — single accepted-line
cancellation (`requestAcceptedLineCancellation`, already reason-coded + free-text) — whole-check
cancellation has no backend action at all (confirmed by the same audit) and was explicitly deferred
as separate, later backend work rather than represented by a button that would do nothing real.

**What changed, concretely**: `_CenterPane`/`_CenterPaneState` (order review) and `_CheckPanel`
(check/split/transfer/finalize) — and the `_StaffEntryScreen` full-screen dialog built earlier today
— are gone, replaced by one `_PosWorkbench`/`_PosWorkbenchState`. The category rail and product
grid from this morning's `_StaffEntryScreen` are promoted into this screen's primary, always-visible
view instead of a secondary push; tapping a card still accumulates into a local cart (never a
real submission per tap — each tap would otherwise mint a separate real order/kitchen ticket per
item, which `_runAction`'s one-call-per-submit model and real kitchen-ticket-per-order shape make
clearly wrong) and "Siparişi Mutfağa Gönder" sends the whole local cart in one real
`submitStaffEntryOrder` call, same as before. Accepted order lines now render directly in the
Adisyon panel (grouped per order, with the existing live `_KitchenStatusBadge` kept directly above
them, unchanged in behavior) instead of only inside a pane; each line carries a single
"İptal Talebi Gönder" icon reusing the exact existing `_ReasonDialog`. The "Onay Bekleyen" and
"İşlemler" sheets reuse `_OrderCard`/`_LineRow`/`_AdjustmentDialog`/the split dialogs/the transfer
dialog verbatim — no backend call, dialog validation, or exception-mapping logic was rewritten,
only where their trigger buttons live. The bottom-of-panel payment button keeps the exact same
3-state logic the old `_CheckPanel` had (`Hesap Aç` → `Ödemeye Hazırla` → `Ödeme Al`/`Ödeme Detayı`),
just relabeled "Ödeme Al" (from "Ödemeye Git") to match the spec's "Ödeme Al / Hesabı Kapat" button.
`_StaffEntryFn`'s typedef widened from a single `(productId, quantity)` pair to a `List` of them,
since `submitStaffEntryOrder`'s `items` parameter already accepted multiple lines — the old dialog
had simply never sent more than one.

**Found and fixed two real layout-overflow bugs while building this** (not test-only workarounds):
the compact account-target dropdown's "Mevcut Müşteri Ara ve Bağla" item overflowed its ~300px-wide
column without `isExpanded: true` + per-item `TextOverflow.ellipsis`; the "Yeni Ürünler Toplamı" /
total `Row` overflowed the same column without wrapping its label in `Expanded`. Both would have
rendered a real yellow/black overflow stripe on an actual POS-width device, not just failed a test.

**Disclosed, known UX limitation, not fixed this pass**: the "Onay Bekleyen" sheet renders
`_OrderCard`s from a plain closure over `widget.view` captured when the sheet opens — if a line is
accepted/rejected while the sheet is still open, the sheet's own display goes stale until it's
closed and reopened (the real action still fires correctly; only the sheet's own re-display doesn't
refresh live). The old always-visible pane never had this problem since it was part of the main
rebuilding tree. Noted here rather than silently shipped as if equivalent — a follow-up could wrap
the sheet's content in something reactive to the outer rebuild if this proves annoying in practice.

### Real menu photos: new per-category asset convention, wired app-wide (not just POS) (2026-11-02)

Requested alongside the first staging commit/CashRegister-REST-recheck/Release-build round: the
product owner is adding real product photos as `assets/menu/<category>/<product>.png`, and asked
for `pubspec.yaml` wiring plus the POS grid's image logic to try the local asset first, falling
back to the placeholder if missing. That exact path didn't exist in the repo yet (confirmed by
search — 0 files); the product owner confirmed via a clarifying question that the folders should be
created now, empty, ready for real PNGs to be dropped in later with no further code changes.

**Found a real regression risk before writing the fallback, not after**: this repo already has an
older, *flat* `assets/images/menu/<imageKey>.png` convention (`MenuImageResolver`, allowlist-based)
under which **53 of today's real catalog products already have a genuine, working photo** (e.g.
`mexifit-bowl`, `abakus-burger`, `grill-salmon-bowl`). A naive "prefer the new per-category path
when available" would have silently regressed every one of those 53 to a placeholder, since the new
folders are empty today. Fixed by making both conventions additive, never either/or:
`MenuImageResolver.resolveCandidates(imageKey, {categoryId})` now returns an ordered **list** (new
convention first when `categoryId` is given, old flat convention second, since the old one is
allowlist-gated and only appears when a real file is confirmed to exist) instead of a single
nullable path. `ProductImageSource.resolveCandidates`/`ProductImage` were widened to match — mirrors
the project's own "state machine of explicit states" discipline, just applied to image fallback —
`ProductImage._buildCandidateChain` tries each candidate via nested `Image.errorBuilder`s, falling
to the real placeholder icon only once every candidate has failed. `MenuImageResolver.resolve`
(single-arg, old convention only) is unchanged for its one remaining caller.

**Deliberately no manually-maintained allowlist for the new convention** (unlike the old one,
which the resolver's own doc comment already says must be "kept in sync... run the test suite after
adding/removing files"): the new per-category candidate is always returned whether or not the file
exists yet, relying entirely on `Image`'s own `errorBuilder` to fall through — this is what lets the
product owner drop a PNG into `assets/menu/<category>/` later with zero code changes, matching what
was actually asked for ("dosya bulunamazsa... fallback yapsın").

**`categoryId` threaded through, app-wide, not only the POS grid** — a deliberate, disclosed small
widening of the literal ask: `ProductImage` gained an optional `categoryId` param (`null` by
default, e.g. for Bowl Builder ingredient cards which have no category concept), and every screen
that renders a real `MenuProduct`'s photo now passes it (`pos_table_workspace_screen.dart`'s POS
grid — the actual ask — plus `menu_screen.dart`, `product_detail_screen.dart` (both the hero image
and the "Bununla İyi Gider" pairing card), `qr_menu_story_bar.dart` (both the story ring and its
quick-view sheet), `pos_cashier_screen.dart`, and Home's `popular_products_section.dart`/
`weekly_editorial_section.dart`). Reusing the one shared `ProductImage`/`MenuImageResolver` seam for
every real-product screen avoids a second, parallel, POS-only image-loading implementation that
would drift from this one — not a UI redesign of any of those screens, purely plumbing one already-
available field (`MenuProduct.categoryId`) through an existing optional parameter.

Folder slugs are derived deterministically from the real `MenuCategory.id` with its `cat_` prefix
stripped (`cat_bowl2` → `bowl2`) — never a second, hand-authored category-name-to-slug table that
could drift from the catalog. Created all 10 active categories' folders
(`assets/menu/{icecekler,kahvalti,tartine,bowl2,tava,salata2,hamburger2,wrap2,makarna2,
atistirmalik2}/`), each with a `.gitkeep` so the still-empty directories are tracked by git and
exist on disk for `pubspec.yaml`/the Flutter asset bundler to find at build time (an undeclared or
missing directory fails `flutter pub get`/the build, not just a silently-ignored no-op).

`flutter analyze` clean (full project). `flutter pub get` succeeded (new asset directories resolve).
`flutter test` full suite green (see this entry's own verification run) — new tests cover:
`resolveCandidates` returning the new path first, the old path second when a real photo already
exists for that key (the regression-prevention case, explicitly), old-path-only when no `categoryId`
is given, and the new convention being skipped for a non-`cat_`-prefixed id; a new `ProductImage`
widget test proves a failed first candidate falls through to a working second candidate without
ever reaching the placeholder.

- `MenuImageResolver.resolveCandidates` rewritten: folder slug = `cat_` prefix **and any trailing
  product-refresh "2" suffix** stripped (`cat_wrap2` → `wrap`, not `wrap2` — matches what the product
  owner actually named the folder). Tries two filenames per category, both already real conventions

  The old allowlist-gated `resolve()`/`_availableImageKeys`/`findMissingImageKeys` were removed —

- **Two real, disclosed-not-silently-fixed mismatches remain in the product owner's own in-progress

### Feature (2026-11-03): POS product customization modal; Bowl protein/sauce/topping add-ons; full menu-PDF allergen/calorie import; allergen pictograms; product search bar

`pos_table_workspace_screen.dart`'s staff product grid previously added every tap straight to the
local cart, ignoring `MenuProduct.modifierGroups`/`nutrition`/`allergens`/`removableIngredients`
entirely (all of which already existed and were already wired for the customer QR menu's
`ProductDetailScreen`/`AddProductToPosOrder`). Added `PosProductCustomizationDialog` — a POS-sized
two-pane modal (not a full-screen push), opened only for a product with a *required* modifier group
or removable ingredients (`_needsCustomization`) so drinks/simple items keep today's single-tap-add;
mirrors `ProductDetailScreen`'s selection/validation rules. `_StaffEntryCartLine` widened to carry
`selectedModifiers`/`excludedIngredients`/`note`; two differently-configured orders of the same
product no longer silently merge quantities. `submitStaffEntryOrder`'s wire payload — which already
had `selectedModifiers`/`note` keys, previously always sent empty — now carries real data; the
backend (`functions/src/submitDineInOrder.ts`) already consumed these fields, so no Cloud Function
change was needed. Added a quick "Not Ekle/Düzenle" popup for pending (not-yet-sent) lines.

**New Bowl modifier groups** (`StandardModifierGroups.bowlProteinAddOnGroup`/`bowlSauceChoiceGroup`/
`bowlToppingsGroup`, BR-BOWL-006–008): İlave Protein, Sos Tercihi, Ekstra Topping, with prices the
product owner confirmed explicitly after being shown they're 3–7x Bowl Builder's own,
separately-VERIFIED ingredient prices for largely the same items — Bowl Builder's pricing was left
untouched. "Sos Tercihi" is flagged as a disclosed simplification: the product owner described "1
dahil, ilave +20 TL" pricing, but the codebase has no selection-order-dependent pricing mechanism
anywhere (same open gap as Bowl Builder's own `BR-BOWL-004`), so every option here is priced flatly
at +20 TL instead.

**Full menu-PDF allergen/calorie import** (BR-BOWL-009 et seq.): the product owner supplied the
verified PDF data for all 21 Bowl, 9 Burger, 20 Tava, and 12 Kahvaltı/Salata products. Matched to
real catalog ids by name (several PDF names are English/shortened variants of the Turkish catalog
names, e.g. "Körili Tavuk Bowl" = `prod_bowl2_kori_soslu_tavuk`) and, for Tava/Burger/Salata2,
cross-checked against calorie values already in the catalog, which matched exactly across all 49 of
those products — strong confirmation the name mapping was correct. 7 of the 21 Bowl products'
existing calorie values were **corrected** (they predated this PDF and were off by a wide margin,
e.g. `prod_bowl2_izgara_somon` 680→850 kcal) — each correction is commented inline with the old value
for anyone auditing the diff. `allergens` added to every matched product (none fabricated — two
Salata2 products, Veggie/Ananas Salad, got no allergens field at all per the PDF's explicit `[]`).

**Allergen pictograms**: `AllergenIcons` maps the five allergens the product owner gave an explicit
icon for (gluten→`Icons.grain`, süt→`Icons.local_drink`, susam→`Icons.spa`, balık→`Icons.phishing`,
yumurta→`Icons.egg_outlined`) — real data for `hardal`/`soya`/`ceviz` exists from the PDF import but
no pictogram was specified for them, so they fall back to a generic icon rather than a guessed
symbol. Replaces the generic "⚠️" triangle on `PosNutritionAllergenBadge` everywhere it's shown (POS
grid card, customization modal); each icon carries a `Tooltip` naming the allergen.

**Product search bar**: a live, client-side name filter above the POS product grid
(`productSearchField`), combined with the existing category filter — no backend change needed.

**Explicitly not built this round, flagged rather than faked**: (1) "Çok Tercih Edilenler" (Top 20
best-sellers) — there is no real sales-history aggregation anywhere in the codebase (`isFeatured` is
a hand-picked static flag, not computed from order counts); building a genuine one needs a new
backend aggregation, which weighted data don't exist. (2) Moving *specific items* from one table's
check to another (as opposed to the whole table, which `transferTable` already does) — no gateway
method or Cloud Function exists for this; it would need a new backend action, not just a UI addition.
Both need a product-owner decision before any code is written for them.

Also out of scope this round (flagged earlier the same day, still unaddressed): item 86/stock
management (close-for-N-hours, price override, hide) has no domain model or persistence anywhere;
manager-PIN-gated cancellation has no PIN/credential primitive anywhere; drag-drop category/product
reordering has nowhere to persist a product-level `sortOrder` (only `MenuCategory` has one, and both
categories and products are compiled-in Dart constants, not a mutable store). All three need an
explicit architecture decision (CLAUDE.md §15) before implementation, not a shallow UI-only pass.

Follow-up to the same day's earlier entry, which deliberately left this unbuilt pending a product-
owner decision on the aggregation approach (BR-POS-001, then UNRESOLVED). Approved design: an
on-demand Cloud Function, no precomputed aggregate, no new Firestore index — built and emulator-
tested (`npm run test:emulator` against a real JDK 21 Firestore/Auth/Functions emulator; the
sandbox's default JDK was 17, which the current `firebase-tools` emulator rejects outright — a
JDK 21 happened to already be installed locally and was pointed to via `JAVA_HOME`).

`functions/src/posTopSellingProducts.ts` (`getTopSellingProducts`) — same auth bar as every other
POS read (`requireStaffPermission` + `requireBranchAccess` + `requireActiveDeviceSession`, mirroring
`posOperationalView.ts`'s own documented rationale for needing all three). Queries `orders` by
`organizationId`/`branchId` equality only; filters to the last 30 days and `accepted`-status lines
**in memory** rather than adding a `timestamps.created` range clause to the query, which would have
needed a new composite index to be created and deployed — exactly the kind of Firebase wiring
CLAUDE.md §5 reserves for its own explicit decision, not something to bolt on while answering "how
do I compute Top 20." 4 new emulator-backed tests (`posTopSellingProducts.test.ts`): quantity
summed/sorted correctly across orders, non-`accepted` lines never counted, an order outside the
30-day window excluded, and the auth-boundary rejection when no active device session exists.

Client side: `PosTopSellingProduct`/`PosOperationalViewGateway.getTopSellingProducts` (real + the
existing `Unavailable` fallback); `topSellingProductsProvider`, a plain (non-`autoDispose`)
`FutureProvider.family<List<PosTopSellingProduct>, PosDeviceContext>` — fetched once per session,
per the approved "oturum boyunca cache" design, invalidated only by an explicit future refresh
action (none exists yet). `PosDeviceContext` gained value `==`/`hashCode` (confirmed nothing relied
on its prior identity semantics) so the `.family` cache key works correctly across rebuilds.

`pos_table_workspace_screen.dart`: the "Tümü" category (and its internal
`_staffEntryAllCategoriesSentinel`, renamed `_staffEntryTopSellersSentinel`) is gone — "Çok Tercih

explicit `LoadingView`/`ErrorView` (retry action)/an explicit "Henüz yeterli satış verisi yok."
empty state — never a silently blank grid for any of the three. **Search behavior changed
alongside this, disclosed, not accidental**: typing in the product search field now overrides the
selected category/Top-20 filter entirely rather than searching only within it — finding a specific
product by name shouldn't require first guessing which tab (or waiting on the Top-20 network call)
it's under. Two pre-existing search tests were updated to match (one's premise — "search works
because 'Tümü' happens to include everything" — no longer holds now that "Tümü" is gone; rewritten
to assert the new, intentional "search overrides category" behavior directly). Added a dedicated
test group: default-selected/no-"Tümü", real backend data rendering, the empty state, and the error
state with its retry button (an `OutlinedButton`, per `ErrorView`'s own implementation — not
`ElevatedButton`, an easy first guess that the test caught).

new `getTopSellingProducts` override to keep compiling, each delegating to `UnimplementedError()`
since neither screen exercises it.

### Feature (2026-11-05): Real Windows USB ESC/POS till-receipt printing

User confirmed real hardware (Windows-installed "POS80 Printer", 80mm USB ESC/POS clone) and asked
for genuine printing — not another disabled placeholder — behind all three existing "Yazdır"
entry points plus a new one on the Masalar grid.

1. **Transport**: `win32`/`ffi` promoted from transitive to direct dependencies.
   `features/printing/data/windows_raw_printer_adapter.dart` sends raw bytes straight to the named
   Windows print queue via `winspool.drv` (`OpenPrinter`/`StartDocPrinter` with the `RAW` datatype/
   `WritePrinter`) — genuinely Windows-only; fails closed with a Turkish message on every other
   platform this app also builds for (Android/iOS/Web), mirroring every other `Unavailable*Gateway`.
   The printer's Windows queue name is a `shared_preferences`-backed setting
   (`ReceiptPrinterSettings`, default `"POS80 Printer"`), not a hardcoded constant — a different
   till can have it installed under a different name.
2. **Receipt content**: `features/pos/domain/receipts/table_receipt_builder.dart` builds a
   `ReceiptDocument` from the same `PosTableOperationalView` the workspace/checkout screens already
   load, totaling against the check's real `computedTotalMinorUnits` (never independently
   recomputed). Per product-owner request, each line prints its standard recipe text
   (`MenuProduct.description`, the same source the menu-PDF ingredient list already comes from)
   plus the order-specific deviation (grouped modifier selections/excluded ingredients/kitchen
   note), mirroring `KitchenTicketMapper`'s own grouping so the printed receipt and the kitchen
   ticket never disagree about what was actually ordered.
3. **Backend**: `getPosTableOperationalView` (`posOperationalView.ts`) now also projects
   `productId`/`modifiers`/`excludedIngredients`/`kitchenNote` per line — already-stored `Order`
   fields this read model simply didn't surface before; purely additive, no existing field changed.
4. **Encoding**: `features/printing/domain/esc_pos_receipt_encoder.dart` — 48-char/80mm layout,
   bold/double-size totals, `GS V 66 0` feed+cut. **Flagged, not vendor-verified**: Turkish text
   uses the Windows-1254 (CP1254) codepage, selected via Epson's documented `ESC t 45` table-select
   byte — the standard convention for this printer class and the same encoding Windows itself uses
   for Turkish, but genuinely untested against the physical unit (`docs/kds_printer_stock_architecture
   .md` §14/§24 already gates a real `PrinterAdapter` on a vendor ESC/POS manual that isn't
   available here). If Turkish characters garble on the real printer, that table-select byte is the
   first thing to check.
5. **Trigger points wired**: the table workspace's quick-action bar "Yazdır" button and the
   "... Diğer" grid tile's "Yazdır" (both previously disabled placeholders) now call the real
   pipeline; a new green quick-print button appears on an occupied/bill-requested card in the
   Masalar grid (`pos_branch_overview_screen.dart`), resolving the table's own open/ready-for-
   payment check itself since the overview summary doesn't carry a checkId.

**Deferred, not done this pass** (reported, not silently dropped): the Masalar grid's category
tabs (Açık Masalar/İç Salon/Bahçe/Rezervasyon/Gel Al Paket/Paket Servis), per-card amount/zone
display, and the blue "open TAHSİLAT directly from the card" quick button all remain outstanding —
the zone/amount fields need their own `PosBranchTableSummary`/`getBranchOverview` extension, and
the reservation/takeaway/delivery tabs need their own scoping decision; this pass focused on the
printer integration the user asked for across three consecutive messages.

### Self-Order QR — Faz 1: Session TTL (2h) + TR/EN guest-locale infrastructure (2026-11-05)

First phase of a 6-faz, user-approved "Masalarda QR Kod ile Sipariş" plan (23 operational rules).
Branch `feature/qr-self-order` (off `phase-7/profile-redesign`'s tip, not `main` — see
`docs/decisions.md` ADR-054 for why). See ADR-054 and `docs/business_rules.md` BR-TABLE-014 for the
full decision record; this entry is the implementation summary.

1. **Session TTL**: `tableGuestSessionConfig.ts`'s `DEFAULT_TABLE_GUEST_SESSION_TTL_HOURS` lowered
   from 6 to **2** — an explicit, user-approved business-rule change, not a silent one. Also fills a
   real pre-existing documentation gap: the file's own comment claimed this was recorded under
   BR-TABLE-005, which has always been "Server-side-only QR token resolution" — no table-session-TTL
   entry actually existed before BR-TABLE-014.
2. **Lock + rescan-extend — investigated, not rebuilt**: before writing any new gate, checked what
   already exists (reuse-first). Found both already correctly implemented ahead of this phase:
   `TableContextBadge` already shows "Oturum süresi doldu — QR kodu tekrar okutun" once the locally-
   held `expiresAt` passes, and `DineInCheckoutScreen._submitOrder` already re-reads the live session
   server-side and blocks submission with a friendly message if it's no longer active. "Re-scan
   extends" also needed no new code: `openTableGuestSession` already mints a brand-new
   `tableGuestSessions` document with a fresh `expiresAt` on every call while reusing the same
   `TableSession`/`GuestSubAccount` — scanning again after expiry just opens a fresh 2-hour session,
   by construction.
3. **TR/EN guest-locale infrastructure (new)**: `features/qr/domain/i18n/{guest_locale,
   qr_flow_strings}.dart` — a small hand-written lookup (not `flutter_localizations`'s ARB/
   `gen-l10n` pipeline, which generates code; CLAUDE.md §2 says this project has no code-generation
   step anywhere). Scope is the dine-in QR entry/status flow only — `TableGuestEntryScreen` (welcome/
   status/error messages), `TableContextBadge` (expired message, waiter/bill tooltips, service-
   request snackbars) — **not** a retroactive translation of the pre-existing customer menu/cart/
   checkout UI, which stays Turkish-only, unchanged. `OpenTableGuestSessionFromQrScan.call` now takes
   an optional `detectedLanguageCode` (default `'tr'`, so no existing caller broke); `TableGuestEntryScreen`
   supplies it from `WidgetsBinding.instance.platformDispatcher.locale.languageCode` (deliberately not
   the bare `dart:ui` `PlatformDispatcher.instance` singleton, which bypasses Flutter's test binding
   entirely and would make the behavior untestable). A manual TR🇹🇷/EN🇬🇧 flag switcher sits in
   `TableContextBadge` (`ActiveTableContextNotifier.setLanguage`, a new method, only ever changes
   `GuestSession.selectedLanguageCode` — `detectedLanguageCode` is never overwritten, per
   `docs/table_qr_architecture.md` §9).
4. **Regression caught and fixed during this pass**: 10 existing `table_guest_entry_screen_test.dart`
   tests asserted Turkish copy without pinning the device locale — once rendering became locale-
   sensitive, Flutter's test environment's own default (`en`) broke them. Fixed properly (not
   papered over) by having those tests explicitly set
   `tester.binding.platformDispatcher.localeTestValue = const Locale('tr')`, since that's what they
   were always implicitly assuming.

### Self-Order QR — Faz 2: allergen pictograms/filter + sold-out ("Tükendi") state (2026-11-05)

Second phase of the same user-approved plan (see Faz 1 above). Binds `MenuProduct.allergens`/
`isAvailable` — both real, pre-existing fields with no prior UI consumer — into the QR menu vitrine.

1. **Allergen pictograms**: `MenuScreen`'s `_ProductListCard` now renders a small `AllergenIcons`
   row (tooltip = the allergen name) under a product's description whenever `allergens` is
   non-empty. `AllergenIcons` itself already existed (product owner, 2026-11-03) but had exactly one
   consumer before this — the POS product-customization dialog — never the customer-facing menu.
2. **Allergen filter row (new)**: `allergenFilterProvider` (`features/menu/presentation/providers/
   allergen_filter_provider.dart`) holds the set of allergens the guest has chosen to exclude;
   `availableAllergensProvider` (`menu_catalog_provider.dart`) derives the sorted, distinct allergen
   list across the active catalog. `MenuScreen` renders one filter chip per allergen beneath the
   category tabs (hidden entirely when the catalog has none) and excludes any product listing a
   selected allergen from the list — an exclusion filter, not a highlight, matching the original
   "alerjen filtreleri" rule.
3. **Sold-out ("Tükendi") state**: an `isAvailable == false` product (`Item 86`) stays visible on the
   menu — never hidden — but its photo dims, its price badge becomes a "Tükendi" pill, and its
   quick-add button is disabled (`onPressed: null`). Applied consistently everywhere a sold-out
   product could otherwise still be bought, not just the card: `ProductDetailScreen`'s "Sepete Ekle"
   button (now "Tükendi" and disabled), `QrMenuStoryBar`'s focused quick-view (its own add button
   hidden, a "· Tükendi" label shown next to the price), and `drinkCrossSellProductsProvider` (sold-
   out drinks no longer offered as a cross-sell chip at all, since that chip has no detail screen of
   its own to show a disabled state on).
4. **"No banner, straight to category tabs" — already satisfied, not rebuilt**: re-checked against
   the 2026-10-29 zero-friction-entry decision (`table_guest_entry_screen.dart`) — there is no
   intermediate welcome/confirm screen in the dine-in QR path; a scan lands directly on `MenuScreen`
   with its category tabs and product vitrine visible. Nothing to change for this rule.

### Self-Order QR — Faz 3: realtime shared table cart (2026-11-05)

Third phase of the same user-approved plan. Two explicit architecture decisions were raised and
resolved before implementation (see ADR — `docs/decisions.md`):
1. **Attribution key**: `addedBySubAccountId` (not `addedByGuestSessionId`) — keyed on the existing
   `guestSubAccounts` deterministic id (`deterministicIdentitySubAccountId`), stable across a QR
   re-scan (Faz 1 mints a fresh `tableGuestSessions` doc every time, which would otherwise make a
   guest's own earlier lines look like "someone else's" after extending their session). Also matches
   `submitDineInOrder.ts`'s own existing per-order-line `subAccountId` attribution.
2. **Write path**: direct client → Firestore writes, gated by `firestore.rules`, not a new Cloud
   Function per mutation — the one table-session-scoped collection in this codebase allowed to work
   this way, because it is deliberately never authoritative: `submitDineInOrder` always re-derives
   real pricing server-side regardless of what a cart line claims.

**Data model**: `tableSessionCarts/{tableSessionId}/lines/{lineId}` — one document per
`(addedBySubAccountId, customizationsKey)` pair (not a single array-holding doc), so two guests
adding the same product concurrently never contend on the same document, and a guest's own repeat
add of an identical configuration merges via an atomic `FieldValue.increment`, no read-before-write
needed. `firestore.rules`: any participant (proven via an `exists()` check against their own already-
created `guestSubAccounts` doc, never a new document) may read the whole shared basket; a write may
only ever claim the caller's own deterministic id, with a field allow-list/shape guard
(`isValidCartLineShape`).

**Dart wiring**: `cartProvider`'s real instance is now `DineInTableCartNotifier` (a `CartNotifier`
subclass) — while `activeTableContextProvider` is null it delegates straight to the unchanged base
class (takeaway/delivery/personal dine-in untouched, byte-for-byte), and the instant a table context
is active it mirrors the live `tableSessionCarts` collection via `.snapshots()` instead of a private
list. `preorderCartProvider` (`features/reservation`) deliberately keeps instantiating the plain base
`CartNotifier` directly, so its own isolated cart never reacts to this. Every mutation
(increment/decrement/remove/clear) is additionally scoped to lines the current device's own sub-
account actually owns — a tap on a tablemate's line (now visible in the shared list) is a safe no-op,
never a cross-guest mutation, matching the security rule regardless.

**Disclosed interim limitation (resolved in Faz 4, not this phase)**: `clearCart()` can only delete
the caller's own lines (the security rule enforces this), so until Faz 4 wires `submitDineInOrder` to
delete the exact submitted lines server-side (Admin SDK, bypasses the ownership lock), a post-
submission clear in this phase alone would not empty a multi-guest cart. `DineInCheckoutScreen`
itself is untouched this phase — it still reads the full shared cart at submission time, which is a
side effect of sharing state, not a Faz 3 feature; Faz 4 ("Hibrit Gönderim") adds the explicit choice.

client_test.dart` (new, 4, pure `deterministicCartLineId` logic), `dine_in_table_cart_notifier_test
.dart` (new, 8, fake-Firestore-backed — ownership guards, snapshot sync, local-mode fallback)). Two
pre-existing test files needed a `tableSessionCartFirestoreClientProvider` fake override added

MenuScreen/building `cartProvider` with an active table context, which would otherwise touch the
real Firestore SDK under `flutter test`. New shared test helper:
`test/features/cart/test_support/fake_table_session_cart_firestore_client.dart`.

**Not run**: `firestore-tests/` emulator suite (`npm run test:emulator`) — same environment limitation

### Self-Order QR — Faz 4: naming (already satisfied), hybrid submission, customer self-cancel (2026-11-05)

Fourth phase of the same plan. Per the user's explicit "no further pausing through Faz 6" direction,
the remaining judgment calls below were made directly (best-practice, matching existing codebase
precedent) rather than raised as new `AskUserQuestion` forks — still disclosed here in full rather
than silently decided.

1. **İsimlendirme ("Adınız nedir?") — investigated, not rebuilt.** `DineInCheckoutScreen` already
   captures a guest's display name reactively: it submits, and only if the server rejects with
   `dineIn/guest-display-name-required` (a guest's genuinely first order at this table — the sub-
   account has no name yet) does it show a name dialog and resubmit with `guestDisplayName` set.
   This already satisfies the rule's literal requirement ("modal on confirm") — the modal appears
   exactly when the guest taps confirm, on whichever submission actually needs a name. Not changed
   to a proactive pre-check: that would mean an extra live read before every single submission for a
   guest who already has a name, for no behavior change.
2. **Hybrid submission** ("Sadece Kendi Ürünlerimi Gönder"/"Tüm Masayı Gönder"): `DineInCheckout
   Screen` gained a `DineInSubmissionScope` toggle, shown ONLY once the shared cart (Faz 3) actually
   has more than one contributor (`_isMultiGuestCart`) — a solo guest has nothing to choose between.
   Defaults to "own items only" (the safer choice — never silently submits, and pays for, a
   tablemate's items without an explicit switch). The scoped subset is computed client-side
   (`_scopedCartItems`) from data Faz 3 already mirrors locally; no new read.
3. **Clearing the shared cart after submission — now fully server-side.** `submitDineInOrder.ts`
   accepts an optional `submittedCartLineIds: string[]` (the exact `tableSessionCarts` document ids
   this submission consumed, computed client-side via the same `deterministicCartLineId` Faz 3
   already uses) and deletes them — via the Admin SDK, inside the SAME transaction as order creation
   — right after the order document is written. This is what actually resolves Faz 3's own disclosed
   interim limitation ("`clearCart()` can only delete the caller's own lines"): the server bypasses
   that ownership lock entirely, which is exactly what lets "Tüm Masayı Gönder" correctly clear a
   tablemate's line a client could never delete directly. `DineInCheckoutScreen` no longer calls
   `clearCart()` at all — the existing `tableSessionCarts` snapshot listener picks up the deletion
   automatically once the transaction commits.
4. **Customer self-cancel** ("mutfak/kasa onayına kadar iptal edebilir"): the first real, server-
   authoritative dine-in order cancellation in this app. New callable `cancelMyPendingDineInOrder`
   mirrors `cancelTakeawayOrder.ts`'s own customer-self-cancel shape closely, with one deliberate
   difference — **no `requireRealCustomer` gate**, since a dine-in guest is very often anonymous;
   ownership is proven via `order.guestAuthUid === request.auth.uid` instead (set for both identity
   types by `submitDineInOrder`, unlike `customerId`, which stays `null` for a guest).
   `pendingConfirmation`-only, exactly the "until kitchen/kasa onayına kadar" boundary; no reason
   code collected, mirroring `cancelTakeawayOrder.ts`'s own identical precedent. Wired into
   `order_detail_screen.dart` for `channel == dineInQr` orders specifically, gated on the REAL
   `lifecycleStatus` enum (not the existing screen's own looser legacy-label `canCancel` check, which
   would have wrongly still allowed a cancel attempt once `confirmed`) — every other channel's
   existing (already-mock, pre-dating this phase) cancel button/dialog is completely untouched.

**Architecture-layering correction made while implementing, not a separate decision point**: the new
cancel gateway was placed under `features/orders/data/` (mirroring `DineInCounterProposalGateway`'s
own precedent), not `features/cart/data/` alongside `SubmitDineInOrderGateway` — `cart` already
imports from `orders` (`OrderModel`/`ordersProvider`), so putting an orders-only concern in `cart`
and importing it back from `orders` would have created this codebase's first feature-import cycle.

### Self-Order QR — Faz 5: çağrı butonları, POS zili, onay→mutfak yazdırma (2026-11-05)

Fifth phase. Per the user's "no further pausing" direction, implementation choices below were made
directly and disclosed here, not raised as new approval-gated questions.

1. **Çağrı butonları**: `ServiceRequestType` extended with the three pre-approved new values
   (`ashtrayOrService`, `clearTable`, `customNote`) alongside the existing `callWaiter`/
   `requestBill`. The rule's 5th UI option, "Çay İste," deliberately reuses `callWaiter` rather than
   adding a 6th backend type — a tea request is just a specific instance of "call the waiter for
   something," the same bucket every other free-form waiter ask already falls into.
   `TableContextBadge`'s two separate icon buttons (waiter/bill) were consolidated into one "Talep
   İlet" button opening a bottom sheet with all 5 options — matching the rule's own "a 'Talep İlet'
   button with options" wording, which describes one entry point, not five standing icons. "Özel
   Not" swaps the sheet's content for a text field + send button in place, never a second stacked
   dialog. `createServiceRequest` (client + `functions/src/serviceRequests.ts`) gained an optional
   `note`, required server-side only when `type === "customNote"`.
2. **POS zili**: `PosBranchOverviewScreen`'s existing 8-second poll now also compares the branch's
   total "needs attention" count (`pendingQrLineCount` + `pendingServiceRequests.length`, summed
   across every table) against the previous poll's own total, and calls `SystemSound.play(SystemSoundType.alert)`
   only when that total went UP — a genuinely new order/çağrı arrived, never when an existing one is
   simply resolved (by this device or another). The POS card-level icon/tooltip for each pending
   request was extended to the 3 new types (`Icons.cleaning_services_outlined`/
   `Icons.sticky_note_2_outlined`, plus a tooltip surfacing the guest's own typed text for
   `customNote`).
3. **Onay → Mutfak Yazdırma — the first real kitchen-ticket printer integration.** `KitchenTicket
   PrintProvider`/`NoOpKitchenTicketPrintProvider` (pre-existing) were explicitly "domain/contract
   only, no printer hardware integration exists" — this phase adds the real one, mirroring the
   already-shipped till-receipt pattern (ADR-053) rather than wiring through that older, now-
   vestigial seam: a new `EscPosKitchenTicketEncoder` (same ESC/POS primitives/WPC1254 codepage as
   `EscPosReceiptEncoder`, kept as its own self-contained file rather than sharing code — the two
   document layouts are genuinely different, and the existing receipt encoder stays byte-for-byte
   unchanged) + a new `PrintKitchenTicket` use case, both reusing the existing, already-approved
   `RawPrinterAdapter`/`ReceiptPrinterSettings` ("POS80 Printer" — the same queue name the 23-rule
   plan's own §6 names for the kitchen ticket too, not a separate device). Wired into
   `PosTableWorkspaceScreen`'s existing per-line accept action: a successful ACCEPT (never a reject)
   re-reads the canonical `Order` and fires a real print, wrapped in a try/catch that swallows any
   printer failure — printing is best-effort additional output, never allowed to block or fail the
   accept action itself, same "no security consequence if absent" framing the `NoOp` provider's own
   doc comment already stated.

   **Required format fully implemented** (Ürün Adı, Adet, Siparişi Veren Kişi Adı, Reçete İçeriği,
   Tercih Notları) — the one previously-missing field, "Siparişi Veren Kişi Adı," needed new
   plumbing: `OrderLineApprovalState` (the existing dine-in-only, index-paired-with-`Order.lines`
   extension point — deliberately kept OUT of the channel-agnostic `OrderLine` itself, matching that
   class's own established pattern) gained `orderedByName`, denormalized by `submitDineInOrder.ts`
   onto every line at order-creation time from the resolved submitter's own name.
   **Disclosed scope decision**: this is the SUBMITTING guest's name on every line, not each
   original cart-adder's own name — correct for "Sadece Kendi Ürünlerimi Gönder" and every solo-
   guest table (the dominant case); a "Tüm Masayı Gönder" order prints the submitter's name on every
   line rather than each contributor's own, since most guests have no name resolvable at all unless
   they've already submitted their own order once this visit. A future pass can revisit this once a
   reliable per-contributor name source exists.

### Self-Order QR — Faz 6: Kapanış/Google review + offline sipariş senkronizasyonu; Canlı Adisyon deliberately deferred (2026-11-06)

Sixth and final phase of this sequential run. Per the user's "no further pausing" direction,
implementation choices below were made directly and disclosed here, not raised as new
approval-gated questions. One of the three sub-items (Canlı Adisyon) could not be honestly
implemented within this pass at all — see its own section below rather than being silently
dropped.

1. **Offline sipariş kuyruklanması (implemented).** New `core/services/connectivity/
   NetworkConnectivityMonitor` (+ real `ConnectivityPlusNetworkMonitor`, wrapping
   `connectivity_plus`) — deliberately a fresh copy of the courier feature's own structurally
   identical class rather than an import of it, to avoid introducing the first `cart`/`qr` →
   `courier` cross-feature dependency. `DineInCheckoutScreen._submitOrder` now checks connectivity
   immediately before the real `submitDineInOrder` call: offline, the submission (exact same
   payload the gateway would have received, including the already-computed
   `submittedCartLineIds`) is written to a new local, durable queue
   (`PendingDineInSubmission` + `DineInOfflineOrderQueueRepository` /
   `SharedPreferencesDineInOfflineOrderQueueRepository`, mirroring POS's own `OfflinePaymentOutbox
   Repository` storage shape but deliberately simpler — no lease/sequence tracking, since each
   entry's own `submissionKey` is already globally idempotent server-side) and the customer sees a
   clear Turkish message instead of a failed network call. A new `SyncOfflineDineInOrders` use
   case replays every queued entry independently (one still-offline/rejected entry never blocks
   the rest) — triggered both on this screen's own `initState` (covers "was already offline, is
   online again by the time this screen next opens") and on a live reconnect signal while the
   screen stays open (`NetworkConnectivityMonitor.onStatusChanged`).
   **Root-cause note on a self-caught regression**: the first working version of this wiring broke
   10 of the pre-existing `dine_in_checkout_screen_test.dart` cases with "pumpAndSettle timed out" —
   traced (systematic-debugging) to the screen's new `initState` calling through to
   `SharedPreferences.getInstance()`/`connectivity_plus`'s platform channel, neither of which is
   mocked in a plain widget test (mirrors why `offline_payment_outbox_repository_test.dart` always
   calls `SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({})` first). Fixed at the root by (a) wrapping the
   screen's own connectivity determination in a try/catch that defaults to "online" when the signal
   is unreadable — strictly safer than silently queueing every order whenever the signal merely
   can't be read — and (b) adding real fakes
   (`_FakeNetworkConnectivityMonitor`/`_FakeDineInOfflineOrderQueueRepository`) wired into every
   existing `pumpWithSeededCart` container, not a symptom-level timeout/skip.
2. **Kapanış + Google review (implemented, with a disclosed signal limitation).** `TableContextBadge`
   now also shows a "Teşekkürler, bizi Google'da değerlendirir misiniz?" prompt (opened via the
   newly-added `url_launcher` dependency) once the table visit ends. **This reuses the badge's own
   pre-existing `isStale` detection (local TTL expiry OR a non-`active` live `tableGuestSessions`
   status) — it does NOT distinguish a genuine staff-initiated closure from mere TTL staleness**,
   because the backend currently has no signal that could: `functions/src/tableGuestSessionConfig
   .ts`'s own doc comment states `tableGuestSessions.status` only ever gets written as `"active"`
   today ("Phase 3 wires the others" — closed/revoked/expired are typed but never actually
   produced by any Cloud Function yet). The staff-side `tableSessions` collection DOES get a real,
   authoritative closure (`tableSessionClosure.ts`'s `releaseTableIfReady`, triggered off `checks`
   reaching a terminal status) — but nothing today propagates that event into the customer-facing
   `tableGuestSessions` document the client actually watches. Wiring that propagation (a new
   Firestore trigger/Cloud Function) is itself a backend architecture change needing its own
   explicit approval, out of scope for this pass. **Also disclosed**: the review link itself is
   `null` by design (`core/config/app_constants.dart`'s new `AppConstants.googleReviewUrl`) — there
   is no real Google Business Profile review URL recorded anywhere in this codebase, and
   fabricating one would ship a broken/misleading link to real customers. The prompt is
   structurally complete and will start appearing the moment that one constant is set to the
   business's real link; no other code change is needed.
3. **Canlı Adisyon (live running bill) — deliberately NOT implemented this pass.** Reasoned through,
   not silently dropped: building this correctly requires a new customer-readable projection of
   `checks`/`checkAllocations` — today `allow read: if false` for any non-staff caller, with the
   only existing read path being the staff-only `getPosTableOperationalView`. Opening any part of
   that financial data to an anonymous table guest is a genuine authorization-model change (new
   Security Rules, likely a new narrow Cloud Function returning a derived, non-sensitive view
   rather than the raw `checks` documents, a new client gateway, new tests) — exactly the kind of
   security-sensitive surface this project's own forward-looking security rules (CLAUDE.md §9) flag
   as needing real server-side authorization, not something to bolt on inside an already-large,
   sequential six-phase pass. **Suggested future-phase shape**: a dedicated `getLiveTableBill`
   callable (mirrors `getPosTableOperationalView`'s own "narrow read-only slice, nothing raw"
   pattern) returning only {lines, running total, applied discounts} for the caller's own active
   `tableSessionId` — re-verified against the same ownership check every other dine-in customer
   callable already uses — rather than any direct client read of `checks`.

### Post-Faz-6 polish: Google review link, physical printer-output fixes (2026-11-06)

Follow-up pass after a real physical print test of the Faz 5 kitchen-ticket printing. Two items
were decided directly by the user (not this codebase guessing), and one investigation changed the
original request before implementing it — all three disclosed here per CLAUDE.md §15.

1. **`AppConstants.googleReviewUrl`** — set to `'https://g.page/r/resto-menum/review'` **by explicit
   user instruction**, who stated it's a placeholder, not yet the business's real verified link.
   Previously `null` by this codebase's own design (no fabricated link) — now non-null because the
   user, not this codebase, supplied the value.
2. **₺ → 'TL' fallback (till receipt)** — `EscPosReceiptEncoder._formatAmount` no longer sends '₺'
   (U+20BA): that symbol has no slot in any classic 8-bit ESC/POS codepage table (every one of them
   predates the Turkish Lira sign), so it always printed as '?' regardless of which codepage was
   selected. 'TL' prints correctly on any table. New test: `esc_pos_receipt_encoder_test.dart` (3
   cases — first test file for this encoder).
3. **Reçete/opsiyon satırları, kitchen ticket** — `EscPosKitchenTicketEncoder` now prints each
   `ingredientSummary` entry and the line note indented with an ASCII `"->"` marker (not a Unicode
   arrow `→` — deliberately: anything outside the encoder's Turkish-letter override table falls back
   to `?`, the exact bug class this pass is otherwise fixing). +1 test case.
4. **Codepage (CP857 vs. WPC1254) — the original request was changed, not silently implemented.**
   The user's physical test found Ş/ğ/ı/İ garbled and asked to switch to CP857/PC857. Investigation
   (web search against Epson's own ESC/POS reference + a Star Micronics manual) found two real
   problems with that specific ask: (a) the `ESC t n` byte index for PC857 is **not standardized
   across printer vendors** — Epson's DM-series uses `n=13`, Star's CBM820 uses `n=8`, and this
   printer's actual brand/model is unknown (same "no vendor manual" gap the original WPC1254
   attempt already disclosed), so guessing a third unverified number carries real risk of selecting
   the wrong table again; (b) more importantly, my own recollection at the time was that **CP857
   historically does not include Ş/ş or Ğ/ğ at all** — switching to it would likely trade today's
   Ş/ğ garbling for a *structural* inability to print Ş/ğ correctly, on exactly the letters the user
   named as broken (this recollection was later found to be WRONG once actually verified — see the
   polish-round-2 entry below). Presented to the user as a Decision Review; they chose to keep
   pursuing a correctly-selected WPC1254 instead. **Not yet implemented**: doing this correctly
   needs either the printer's actual model name or its self-test page — blocked on that input, not
   on any remaining code work; the current `ESC t 45` byte is left unchanged pending it.

`flutter analyze` (whole project): clean (one pre-existing-pattern `info`, not an error, on
`AppConstants.googleReviewUrl`'s intentionally-nullable type). `flutter test` (whole project): 3936

### Post-Faz-6 polish, round 2: self-test-page-driven codepage fallback (2026-11-06)

The user ran the printer's own self-test page and reported: default codepage is CP437 (confirms why
every Turkish letter was garbled pre-WPC1254), and gave the printer's own `ESC t 19` index for its
PC857 table as a fallback if `ESC t 45` (WPC1254, kept as the primary/default) doesn't render
correctly. Two things were verified rather than guessed this round, using `iconv-lite` (already a
`functions/node_modules` dependency — no new tool added) as a real, authoritative codec reference
instead of memory or web-search fragments:

- **CP857 DOES include Ş/ş/Ğ/ğ** (at 0x9E/0x9F/0xA6/0xA7) — the previous entry's "CP857 lacks
  Turkish Ş/Ğ" concern was a real finding at the time (based on fragmentary/uncertain recollection,
  disclosed as such) but turned out to be **incorrect** once actually checked against a real codec.
  Corrected here rather than left standing.
- **PC857's 0x80–0xFF byte layout is NOT Latin-1-compatible** (unlike WPC1254, which mostly is) —
  the existing "pass through runes ≤0xFF, override 6 specific letters" shortcut is only valid for
  WPC1254; the PC857 path needed its own explicit table (verified: Ç=0x80, ç=0x87, Ö=0x99, ö=0x94,
  Ü=0x9A, ü=0x81, Ğ=0xA6, ğ=0xA7, İ=0x98, ı=0x8D, Ş=0x9E, ş=0x9F) with only plain ASCII (≤0x7F)
  safe to pass through unmapped.

**Implemented**: new `ReceiptCodepage` enum (`lib/features/printing/domain/receipt_codepage.dart`,
`wpc1254`/`pc857`) accepted as an optional parameter by both `EscPosReceiptEncoder.encode`/
`EscPosKitchenTicketEncoder.encode` (default `wpc1254`, so every existing call site/test is
unaffected). `ReceiptPrinterSettings` (`pos_workspace_providers.dart`) gained a persisted `codepage`
getter/setter mirroring `printerName`'s exact `shared_preferences` pattern. **Disclosed, deliberate
scope limit**: there is no UI toggle for this setting yet (same as `printerName`, which also has
none) — ESC/POS has no feedback channel, so software cannot auto-detect which table rendered
correctly; switching requires calling `setCodepage` once a physical test confirms which table this
unit actually needs. `PrintTableReceipt`/`PrintKitchenTicket` and their two UI call sites
(`print_table_receipt_action.dart`, `pos_table_workspace_screen.dart`) now thread
`printerSettings.codepage` through on every print.

New tests: `pos_workspace_providers_test.dart` (new, 3 cases — default/round-trip/persistence-
across-restart, mirroring `offline_payment_outbox_repository_test.dart`'s own pattern), +2 cases
each in `esc_pos_receipt_encoder_test.dart`/`esc_pos_kitchen_ticket_encoder_test.dart` (codepage
byte selection + PC857 Turkish-letter byte verification). `flutter analyze`: clean. `flutter test`
(whole project): 3942 passing, 0 failures (+6 over 3936).

### PAX A910SF ECR/GMP-3 "Kredi Kartı" collection — honest scaffolding, real protocol still blocked (2026-11-06)

Full reasoning/decisions in `docs/decisions.md` ADR-059 — summary here. The user asked for a direct
TCP-socket ECR/GMP-3 integration to a physical PAX A910SF terminal; this is **not implemented**, by
design, because `docs/payment_cash_fiscal_architecture.md` §14/§21/§22 and ADR-032 ("Locked") already
gate exactly this device as a `CONTROLLED_EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCY` — no vendor protocol detail without
official PAX SDK/GMP-3 documentation, real-hardware acceptance testing is a hard gate. Confirmed
with the user before writing any code; they chose to build everything else.

**Also found and resolved before implementing**: this codebase has two parallel, non-interoperating
payment subsystems — the real/reachable one (`PosCheckoutScreen` → `PaymentGateway
.recordPaymentAttempt`, server-mediated) and an orphaned one (`PosPaymentScreen`/
`PaymentSessionController`/`PaymentService`/the `PaymentProviderAdapter` registry, reached only via
`PosCashierScreen`, which nothing in the app's real navigation opens — this is where the pre-existing
`PaxTebTerminalAdapter` stub actually lives). Confirmed with the user: extend the real, reachable
screen, not the dead one.

**Implemented** (Flutter-only, nothing on the backend): `PaxGmp3TerminalClient` interface +
`UnavailablePaxGmp3TerminalClient` (`lib/features/pos/data/pax_gmp3_terminal_client.dart`) — always
resolves "unavailable," exactly like every other not-yet-wired boundary in this codebase.
`PaxTerminalSettings` (IP/port, persisted — default `192.168.1.86`/`9000` per the operator's own
setup notes) added to `pos_workspace_providers.dart` alongside `ReceiptPrinterSettings`. New "PAX
Cihazı ile Oku" button in `PosCheckoutScreen`'s `_TenderPanel`, visible only when the `card` tender
chip is selected — the existing `_kSandboxOnlyTenderTypes` release-build gate on `card` is
unchanged, so the whole PAX flow stays exactly as reachable/unreachable as `card` already was.
Tapping it opens a "POS Cihazından Kart Bekleniyor..." modal (countdown + "İptal") that calls the
client and shows its honest result — never fabricates a success/decline, never calls
`onSubmitTender` for an outcome with nothing real to record.

**Explicitly deferred, not silently dropped**: extending `recordPaymentAttempt` (Flutter +
`functions/src/paymentEngine.ts`) to accept a client-reported external terminal authorization.
Beyond being premature ahead of a working adapter, naively trusting a client-supplied "approved"
result with no independent server-side verification is a real fraud vector this codebase's existing
trusted-device gate alone doesn't fully close — the actual trust/verification model (end-of-day
reconciliation against the acquirer's settlement report, ideally a signed terminal response once
real GMP-3 docs exist) is its own dedicated decision for once a real adapter exists to call.

**Found and disclosed, not fixed (pre-existing, out of scope)**: `PosCheckoutScreen`'s
`_SummaryPanel`/`_AmountRow` has no `Expanded`/`Flexible` wrapping and overflows for an open
(non-completed) session at common narrow/tablet widths — never caught before because no existing
test rendered that branch (only the `completed` view, a different widget tree, had coverage).

New tests: `pos_checkout_screen_test.dart` (+3 cases). `flutter analyze`: clean. `flutter test`
(whole project): see the final gate run below for the updated count.
